newsitem.title: USA: AA Cargo sees normal business by Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: AA Cargo sees normal business by Wednesday.

text.p: Cargo volumes at American Airlines should be back to near normal by tomorrow after last week's confrontation with pilots, Mark Najarian, vice-president of AA Cargo sales said.

Almost as soon as the presidential back-to-work order came early Saturday, suspending the pilots' right to strike for 60 days, most accounts began tendering freight again, Najarian told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Most large accounts stuck with American up to the point Friday when it began cancelling some flights to ensure an orderly shutdown of operations.
For that reason, said Najarian, no long term fallout from the dispute is expected.

Without Monday's Presidents' Day Holiday in the U.S., traffic levels might have been close to normal by today, he said, but since few U.S. shippers were moving freight Monday, that will slow the recovery by 24 hours.

Also, freight tendered in some overseas markets has to clear customs there and move to the U.S. along prescribed routings, which means some of American's import lanes will not be back to normal until Wednesday, he added.
American is offering discounts of up to 45 percent -- mainly on domestic narrowbody flights and some transcontinental and international flights to stimulate demand.
"On some international markets we're going to be doing some promotional pricing as we need to," said Najarian, adding this is as much a response to general market conditions as the strike.
Najarian told Reuters that AA Cargo's international discounts will vary by gateway, will only affect some routes, and will not necessarily last to the end of the month.
"If you called down to Miami today, they'd probably give you some special rates to Argentina for a couple of days until they get their volumes up again," he said.
"If you called Chicago, they'd probably give you some special rates to Zurich."
Domestically, the airline's 45 percent discount will be available to all customers until February 28 for most narrowbody flights.

Najarian said most of American's competitors were "very responsible" in their response to the strike threat, helping American's customers make alternate arrangements. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
